title: Eval Signals: routing, contextual dedupe, and rollback affordances in Console (Slack + PagerDuty)
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Teams are seeing noisy eval regression alerts when config or model changes are rolled out. Alerts currently fire per-eval-result without reliable attribution to the triggering change (model version, quantization profile, batching config, or prompt set). This causes paging noise and slow incident resolution.

Goal: Deliver a Console feature that links Evals results to configuration and model changes, routes contextualized alerts to the correct Slack channels and PagerDuty escalation policies, and reduces duplicate/related alerts by grouping at the change-signature level. Provide operators with one-click context (change diff, sample failing prompts, recent rollout) and an optional rollback action surface for Dedicated/Private customers.

Scope:
- Backend: attach immutable change signatures to eval runs (model hash + config delta hash + prompt-set id). Generate a canonical "signal id" for grouping.
- Routing: map signal metadata to destination (team Slack webhook, PagerDuty service + severity) via Console routing rules UI. Severity mapping based on eval metric delta thresholds and customer impact flag.
- Dedupe: server-side suppression window (configurable per-project) that groups alerts with same signal id and suppresses repeated notifications for X minutes, while retaining a single aggregated alert in Console.
- Console UI: new "Signal timeline" and "Change attribution" pane on eval detail that shows linked deployments, diffs, sample failures, and rollout IDs. Add a "Create PD Incident" and "Rollback" CTA for teams with appropriate permissions.
- Integrations: Slack notifications with contextual attachments (top 3 failing prompts, delta chart, link to eval run). PagerDuty integration should trigger on severity >= critical with deduplicated incident keys and include change signature for automatic correlation.

Out of scope for this ticket: automated model rollback orchestration across Dedicated capacity (requires infra/eng coordination). Full per-customer RBAC for rollback will land in a follow-up (PM-7349).
acceptance_criteria: Console shows a "Signal timeline" on eval detail that lists model/config changes (with timestamps) linked to that eval run.
Each eval run produced after a config/model change is stamped with a deterministic "signal id" computed from model hash + config-delta-hash + prompt-set id.
Alert routing rules allow mapping of signal attributes to Slack channel webhook and PagerDuty service (UI and API).
Notifications to Slack contain the top 3 failing prompts, metric delta, and a direct link to the eval in Console.
PagerDuty alerts use a deterministic dedupe key derived from the signal id so repeated failures during the suppression window correlate to the same incident.
Server-side dedupe/suppression groups identical signal ids for a configurable default window of 30 minutes and surface a single aggregated alert in Console.

Operators with permissions see a "Rollback" CTA that creates an internal rollback request ticket (stubbed UI action that links to ENG-xxxx for manual rollback flow) and logs the action in eval audit trail.
End-to-end integration tested: Slack message posted, PagerDuty incident created, and repeated eval failures within the suppression window do not create duplicate PagerDuty incidents in staging.
Documentation exists in Confluence describing the routing rule fields, signal id generation algorithm, and recommended thresholds for severity mapping.
notes: Decision: use a hashed "signal id" composed as sha256(model_version || '|' || sorted(config_delta) || '|' || prompt_set_id). This gives stable grouping even when multiple deploys reference the same model/config set.
Tradeoff: choosing a 30-minute default suppression reduces noise but may hide fast-failing regressions; we expose suppression window in routing rules so teams can tune to 5/30/60 minutes.

Privacy: notifications will avoid sending full customer data. Only sample prompts (redacted) and metric aggregates will be included. Security reviewed with privacy team on 2025-01-20 (no PII in payloads).
Rollback UI is a soft action (creates a ticket in the infra ops queue) in this phase — fully automated rollback to be scoped in a later epic with ENG and SRE.
Edge cases: when two separate changes produce identical signal ids (unlikely but possible), alerts will be grouped; Console will list both deploys in the timeline to aid attribution.
Design: mockups created and approved; see Confluence link and mock image in PR. UX agreed with Design (Anya Patel) on 2025-01-22.
QA: include unit tests for signal id generation and e2e integration test that simulates a failing eval run after a model bump.
